saints.name: St. Stanislaus
saints.title: Bishop and Martyr
saints.shortBlurb: The Bishop of Kraków slain at the altar for rebuking a king, and the patron of Poland…
biography: Born at Szczepanów in 1030, the only son of the nobles Wielisław and Bogna, Stanislaus studied at Gniezno and, by tradition, at Paris. Ordained by Bishop Lambert II, he rose to be canon, preacher, and vicar-general of Kraków, and on the bishop's death in 1072 was chosen his successor at the command of Pope Alexander II.

One of the first native Poles to hold a bishopric, he restored Gniezno's metropolitan see, making possible Bolesław II's coronation as king in 1076. Yet he did not spare that king: rebuking Bolesław the Bold for his crimes, he at last excommunicated him, whereupon the royal court condemned the bishop to death for treason.

On 11 April 1079, as he celebrated Mass in the chapel of Saint Michael on Skałka outside Kraków, the king's men dared not touch him and Bolesław struck him down himself; the body was hacked to pieces. The outrage cost Bolesław his throne.

Canonized by Innocent IV at Assisi in 1253, he became patron of Poland; Poles read in the legend of his scattered and reunited members a prophecy that their riven nation would be made whole, and their kings were crowned kneeling before his shrine at Wawel.
saints.knownFor: Dying a martyr for the Church's freedom against a king.

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 11 April
